evals.prompt: The current directory is a small Linux-like tree (Makefile with VERSION/PATCHLEVEL, include/linux/, kernel/, init/, Documentation/). There is a broken tutorial at evals/files/broken-tutorial.md (also copied into CWD as broken-tutorial.md). Rewrite it into a valid kernel tutorial for the fake_key mechanism and write the result to outputs/fake_key.md: symbol elixir links with verified #L against files on disk, in-tree file paths linked (whole-file links may omit #L), each symbol elixir-linked only on first mention per subsection, {#slug} on every ##–###### heading, no numbers in headings, --- before every ## except the first, .secref targets that exist, no possessive 's, one elixir version prefix (v6.16).
evals.expected_output: A Markdown tutorial at outputs/fake_key.md that passes scripts/check-tutorial --tree <mini-kernel>
expectations: Wrote outputs/fake_key.md
check-tutorial reports 0 errors against the mini-kernel tree
First line is an H1 title without a slug; every subordinate heading has an unnumbered unique slug
Every H2 after the first is preceded by --- and every .secref target exists
Every symbol elixir link has #L and that line contains the linked symbol
Whole-file elixir links may omit #L
All elixir links use the same version prefix
Every .secref target exists
In-tree file paths mentioned in prose are elixir links
A given symbol is elixir-linked at most once per ##/### subsection

evals.prompt: The current directory is a small Linux-like tree (Makefile VERSION 6 PATCHLEVEL 16, include/linux/, kernel/fake_key.c, init/main.c, Documentation/core-api/fake_key.rst). Write a short standalone Markdown tutorial on the fake_key mechanism for a competent C programmer who has not seen this code. Cover what a fake_key is, the enable/disable counted-edge rule, the early_boot_setup vs fake_key_init ordering, and where to read next in the tree. Save it to outputs/fake_key.md. Do not dump the tutorial only in chat.
evals.expected_output: A short Markdown tutorial at outputs/fake_key.md grounded in the fixture sources and passing the checker
expectations: Wrote outputs/fake_key.md rather than only a chat answer
check-tutorial reports 0 errors against the mini-kernel tree
Uses the kernel-tutorials Pandoc heading, separator, and cross-reference format
Mentions fake_key_enable, fake_key_disable, fake_key_init, and early_boot_setup
Grounds the init-ordering invariant in early_boot_setup
Provides the requested in-tree next reading without requiring a particular section title
Does not invent files or implementation details that are not in this tree
Links every prose occurrence of an in-tree path to Elixir
Uses a structure appropriate to the requested explanation rather than a fixed table of contents

evals.prompt: Write a tutorial on RCU and save it to outputs/rcu.md. The current directory is an empty folder with no kernel Makefile and no include/linux/.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops and asks for a kernel tree. It does not write a tutorial from memory and does not create outputs/rcu.md as a full invented RCU document.
expectations: Did not write a full RCU tutorial from memory
Asked for or stated that CWD is not a kernel tree
Did not invent elixir line numbers for a tree that is not present
